title: Five situations, five frameworks
intro: Not five stock lists for five personalities — five ways of thinking for the situations every investor actually meets.

steps.title: Against the personality quiz
steps.body:
'Are you a growth chaser or a safety seeker?' sounds useful and quietly misses the point. Good investing isn't a label that fits your temperament — it's **a handful of ways of thinking that work in nearly any market, any year, for any investor.**

Behind all five: thirty years of scoring every listed company on **Quality, Growth, Valuation and Momentum**, each out of 10.

steps.title: The five
steps.body:
1. **The fallen stock** — a bad year is not a permanent verdict; the screen hunts compounders that kept growing through past slowdowns.
2. **Earned momentum** — momentum is real; the framework separates momentum earned by results from momentum running on sentiment.
3. **Dividend honesty** — profits can be presented favorably (revenue timing, depreciation choices); sustained cash out the door cannot.
4. **The QGV alignment** — the rare business where all three show up at once.
5. **The compromise audit** — most investors give one up without noticing (next step).

points.label: − Growth
points.note: Castrol India: ROC above 40%, dominant brand, every quality box ticked — and a flat decade. The market matured; EVs capped the future. Quality without growth persists; it doesn't compound. (Colgate rhymes.)

points.label: − Valuation
points.note: HDFC Bank: RoE >15% every year since 2006 (one exception), double-digit growth throughout — the honest answer that a near-perfect record can't rescue an entry price that already assumed it.

points.label: − Quality
points.note: Growth + cheapness without quality is the turnaround lottery — the winners table remembers the few that worked.

steps.title: Using them Monday
steps.body:
Each framework ends in a checkable question: did earnings grow through the last two corrections? Is the rally out-running results? Is the payout covered by cash, not adjustments? What am I paying for the record?

> [!tip] Diagnose the **situation** in front of you, not your temperament — the situation picks the framework.

recap:
**Frameworks for situations, not labels for people.**

- Fallen compounders, earned momentum, dividend honesty, QGV alignment.
- Castrol: quality alone persists, doesn't compound. HDFC Bank: quality+growth can't rescue the price.
- Every framework ends in a checkable question.
- The situation picks the tool.
